summary: Clackamas County butte tower south of Molalla: 1936 district records give the build year (register says 1947); destroyed with footings left by 1970; sold 1968.

facts.design: 90-foot tower with an L-4 cab and a cabin (register); 90-foot wooden L-6 tower with a cabin (firelookout.com); 100-foot creosoted ring-connected tower with a 7x7 cab (1936 district records)
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed; a 1970 National Geodetic Survey recovery note says the footings were still in place. Abandoned 1965; site sold 1968.
facts.agency: Clackamas County, Oregon (register); Oregon Department of Forestry, Clackamas-Marion FPA (district pages and firelookout.com)

events.note: Construction of a 100-foot creosoted tower with a 7x7 cab started July 15, 1936; the district annual report credits the CCC with the tower, a one-room station and a garage
Winds of the Columbus Day storm destroyed the 7x7 cab
A new 7x7 cab was put on the tower
Register and firelookout.com both say the lookout was abandoned in 1965
Site sold for $5,600 according to the district annual report
NGS recovery note: tower destroyed, footings in place

evidence.supports: 90-foot tower with L-4 cab and cabin built in 1947; abandoned 1965; gone
evidence.quote: A 90 foot tower with a L-4 cab and a cabin were built on the site in 1947. The lookout was abandoned in 1965 and is gone.

evidence.supports: Clackamas County administers the site (register: Administered by Clackamas County, Oregon)
site is about 12 miles south of Molalla
90-foot wooden L-6 tower and cabin dated 1940; abandoned 1965; gone
evidence.quote: 1940: 90' wooden L-6 tower, cabin. Abandoned 1965. Gone.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com names the Oregon Department of Forestry as agency
March 1936 item in The Forest Log: a 92-foot tower and guard station planned at Myers Butte
evidence.quote: March 1936: The erection of a 92-foot lookout tower and guard station, similar to the one at House mountain, is contemplated at Myers butte as soon as a construction crew is picked. (The Forest Log)

evidence.supports: construction of a 100-foot creosoted tower with a 7x7 cab started July 15, 1936
evidence.quote: A 100-foot creosoted ring connected tower with a 7 x 7 cab was started July 15, 1936.

evidence.supports: 1936 district annual report credits the CCC with a 100-foot tower, one-room station and garage
evidence.quote: 1936: The CCC constructed a 100 foot lookout tower and one room station and garage on Myers Butte. 7S 2E Sec 13. (Clackamas-Marion District Annual Report)

evidence.supports: 1962 Columbus Day storm destroyed the 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: 1962: The 7 x 7 cab was destroyed by the winds of the Columbus Day storm.

evidence.supports: 1963 replacement 7x7 cab put on the tower
evidence.quote: 1963: The 7 x 7 cab was replaced on the Myers Butte tower.
1968: The Myers Butte Lookout site was sold for $5600.00.

evidence.supports: 1970 National Geodetic Survey recovery note: tower destroyed, footings in place
evidence.quote: RECOVERY NOTE BY NATIONAL GEODETIC SURVEY 1970 ... THE LOOKOUT TOWER HAS BEEN DESTROYED, BUT THE FOOTINGS ARE IN PLACE.

evidence.supports: history page names the Oregon Department of Forestry as the agency

corrections.why: Construction started July 15, 1936 per the investment record, and the 1936 district annual report credits the CCC with the 100-foot tower. The 1947 date comes from the register only; firelookout.com gives 1940.
28.0 m is 92 feet, the height in the 1936 planning item. The register and firelookout.com both give 90 feet as built.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 1947 and firelookout.com says 1940, but the 1936 planning item and district annual report describe construction starting July 15, 1936. The story uses 1936 and reports the other dates.

Register and firelookout.com say 90 feet, the 1936 planning item says 92 feet, and the 1936 district annual report says 100 feet. The story gives the 90-foot figure from the register and firelookout.com and notes the 100-foot figure.
Register lists Clackamas County; firelookout.com and the district pages name the Oregon Department of Forestry, Clackamas-Marion FPA.

notes_for_editor: Build year and height disagree across all three sources. The story follows the 1936 district records, the only dated primary-style evidence, but the 1936 correction is a judgment call for the editor. No source describes the site today, its ownership after the 1968 sale, or public access; the 1970 NGS note is the latest physical record. No staffing history is in these sources, so staffing is omitted.
